The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

XZ Utils
========

Overview
--------

XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus
command-line tools. The native file format is the .xz format, but
also the legacy .lzma format is supported. The .xz format supports
multiple compression algorithms, which are called "filters" in the
context of XZ Utils. The primary filter is currently LZMA2. With
typical files, XZ Utils create about 30% smaller files than gzip.

The .xz format supports multiple compression algorithms. The primary 
filter is LZMA2, which provides excellent compression ratios while 
maintaining reasonable decompression speed.

Key Features
------------

- Compresses data into the .xz format (and legacy .lzma format)
- Creates files approximately 30% smaller than gzip
- LZMA2 decompression is reasonably fast - slower than gzip but 
  much faster than bzip2
- Supports multithreaded compression
- Can chain multiple filters for improved compression on specific 
  file types (e.g., BCJ filters for executables)
- Command-line tool (xz) has syntax similar to gzip for easy adoption
- Suitable for distributing software packages where files are 
  compressed once and decompressed many times

Usage
-----

The main command-line tool is 'xz'. Common usage:

Compress a file:
    xz file.txt
    (creates file.txt.xz and removes file.txt)

Decompress a file:
    xz -d file.txt.xz
    or: unxz file.txt.xz
    (creates file.txt and removes file.txt.xz)

Keep the original file:
    xz -k file.txt

Compress to stdout:
    xz -c file.txt > file.txt.xz

Decompress to stdout:
    xz -dc file.txt.xz
    or: xzcat file.txt.xz

Test compressed file integrity:
    xz -t file.txt.xz

List information about compressed file:
    xz -l file.txt.xz

Set compression level (1-9, default 6):
    xz -6 file.txt     # balanced
    xz -9 file.txt     # maximum compression (slow, uses more memory)
    xz -1 file.txt     # fast compression

Use multithreaded compression:
    xz -T4 file.txt    # use 4 threads
    xz -T0 file.txt    # use all available CPU cores

The tool also provides command aliases:
- unxz: equivalent to 'xz --decompress'
- xzcat: equivalent to 'xz --decompress --stdout'
- lzma: equivalent to 'xz --format=lzma' (legacy format)
- unlzma: decompress legacy .lzma files
- lzcat: decompress legacy .lzma files to stdout

Additional Information
----------------------

For detailed information about the .xz file format specification, 
see doc/xz-file-format.txt

For frequently asked questions, see doc/faq.txt

For historical information about the format, see doc/history.txt

For legacy .lzma format information, see doc/lzma-file-format.txt

License
-------

XZ Utils are released under multiple licenses. See the COPYING file
and individual COPYING.* files for details.

Contact
-------

Home page: https://tukaani.org/xz/
Email: xz@tukaani.org
IRC: #tukaani on Libera Chat
GitHub: https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz
---
XZ Utils Release History
=========================

This file has been simplified to show only user-facing changes.
For full development history, see the original repository.

The XZ Utils project provides data compression tools using the LZMA2
algorithm and the .xz file format. Each release has included various
improvements to compression performance, decompression speed, and
command-line tool functionality.

Major features added over the project's history include:
- Multithreaded compression support
- Various compression filters (BCJ, Delta, etc.)
- Improved memory efficiency
- Enhanced compatibility with various platforms
- Support for the .lz format (lzip decompression)
- Numerous command-line options for fine-tuning compression

For the most current version and detailed release notes,

XZ Utils FAQ
============

Q:  What do the letters XZ mean?

A:  Nothing. They are just two letters, which come from the file format
    suffix .xz. The .xz suffix was selected, because it seemed to be
    pretty much unused. It has no deeper meaning.


Q:  What are LZMA and LZMA2?

A:  LZMA stands for Lempel-Ziv-Markov chain-Algorithm. It is the name
    of the compression algorithm designed by Igor Pavlov for 7-Zip.
    LZMA is based on LZ77 and range encoding.

    LZMA2 is an updated version of the original LZMA to fix a couple of
    practical issues. In context of XZ Utils, LZMA is called LZMA1 to
    emphasize that LZMA is not the same thing as LZMA2. LZMA2 is the
    primary compression algorithm in the .xz file format.


Q:  There are many LZMA related projects. How does XZ Utils relate to them?

A:  7-Zip and LZMA SDK are the original projects. LZMA SDK is roughly
    a subset of the 7-Zip source tree.

    p7zip is 7-Zip's command-line tools ported to POSIX-like systems.

    LZMA Utils provide a gzip-like lzma tool for POSIX-like systems.
    LZMA Utils are based on LZMA SDK. XZ Utils are the successor to
    LZMA Utils.

    There are several other projects using LZMA. Most are more or less
    based on LZMA SDK. See <https://7-zip.org/links.html>.


Q:  Why is liblzma named liblzma if its primary file format is .xz?
    Shouldn't it be e.g. libxz?

A:  When the designing of the .xz format began, the idea was to replace
    the .lzma format and use the same .lzma suffix. It would have been
    quite OK to reuse the suffix when there were very few .lzma files
    around. However, the old .lzma format became popular before the
    new format was finished. The new format was renamed to .xz but the
    name of liblzma wasn't changed.


Q:  Do XZ Utils support the .7z format?

A:  No. Use 7-Zip (Windows) or p7zip (POSIX-like systems) to handle .7z
    files.


Q:  I have many .tar.7z files. Can I convert them to .tar.xz without
    spending hours recompressing the data?

A:  In the "extra" directory, there is a script named 7z2lzma.bash which
    is able to convert some .7z files to the .lzma format (not .xz). It
    needs the 7za (or 7z) command from p7zip. The script may silently
    produce corrupt output if certain assumptions are not met, so
    decompress the resulting .lzma file and compare it against the
    original before deleting the original file!


Q:  I have many .lzma files. Can I quickly convert them to the .xz format?

A:  For now, no. Since XZ Utils supports the .lzma format, it's usually
    not too bad to keep the old files in the old format. If you want to
    do the conversion anyway, you need to decompress the .lzma files and
    then recompress to the .xz format.

    Technically, there is a way to make the conversion relatively fast
    (roughly twice the time that normal decompression takes). Writing
    such a tool would take quite a bit of time though, and would probably
    be useful to only a few people. If you really want such a conversion
    tool, contact Lasse Collin and offer some money.


Q:  I have installed xz, but my tar doesn't recognize .tar.xz files.
    How can I extract .tar.xz files?

A:  xz -dc foo.tar.xz | tar xf -


Q:  Can I recover parts of a broken .xz file (e.g. a corrupted CD-R)?

A:  It may be possible if the file consists of multiple blocks, which
    typically is not the case if the file was created in single-threaded
    mode. There is no recovery program yet.


Q:  Is (some part of) XZ Utils patented?

A:  Lasse Collin is not aware of any patents that could affect XZ Utils.
    However, due to the nature of software patents, it's not possible to
    guarantee that XZ Utils isn't affected by any third party patent(s).


Q:  Where can I find documentation about the file format and algorithms?

A:  The .xz format is documented in xz-file-format.txt. It is a container
    format only, and doesn't include descriptions of any non-trivial
    filters.

    Documenting LZMA and LZMA2 is planned, but for now, there is no other
    documentation than the source code. Before you begin, you should know
    the basics of LZ77 and range-coding algorithms. LZMA is based on LZ77,
    but LZMA is a lot more complex. Range coding is used to compress
    the final bitstream like Huffman coding is used in Deflate.


Q:  I cannot find BCJ and BCJ2 filters. Don't they exist in liblzma?

A:  BCJ filter is called "x86" in liblzma. BCJ2 is not included,
    because it requires using more than one encoded output stream.


Q:  I need to use a script that runs "xz -9". On a system with 256 MiB
    of RAM, xz says that it cannot allocate memory. Can I make the
    script work without modifying it?

A:  Set a default memory usage limit for compression. You can do it e.g.
    in a shell initialization script such as ~/.bashrc or /etc/profile:

        XZ_DEFAULTS=--memlimit-compress=150MiB
        export XZ_DEFAULTS

    # Stream: Header 12 bytes? 6 magic + 2 flags + 4 crc
    # Actually Stream Header: Magic 6 bytes FD 37 7A 58 5A 00, then Stream Flags 2 bytes, then CRC32 4 bytes = 12 bytes
    # Then blocks, then Index, then Footer 12 bytes: CRC32 4 + Backward Size 4 + Flags 2 + Magic 2 (59 5A)
    # We need to parse all streams (possibly concatenated with padding)
    offset=0
    streams=[]
    total_comp=len(content)

2.1.1.1. Header Magic Bytes

        The first six (6) bytes of the Stream are so called Header
        Magic Bytes. They can be used to identify the file type.

            Using a C array and ASCII:
            const uint8_t HEADER_MAGIC[6]

            be erroneously detected as being in .lzma format, in which
            the first byte is in the range [0x00, 0xE0].

        settings so that the LZMA2 encoder can take advantage of its

        The output of the last filter in the chain is stored to the
        Compressed Data field, which is is guaranteed to be aligned

          - speed, if the filtered data is handled multiple bytes at

            because accessing aligned data in computer memory is

          - compression ratio, if the output data is later compressed

5.2. Security

        If filters would be allowed to be chained freely, it would be
        possible to create malicious files, that would be very slow to
        decode. Such files could be used to create denial of service
        attacks.

        Slow files could occur when multiple filters are chained:

            v   Compressed input data
            |   Filter 1 decoder (last filter)
            |   Filter 0 decoder (non-last filter)
            v   Uncompressed output data

        The decoder of the last filter in the chain produces a lot of
        output from little input. Another filter in the chain takes the
        output of the last filter, and produces very little output
        while consuming a lot of input. As a result, a lot of data is
        moved inside the filter chain, but the filter chain as a whole
        gets very little work done.

        To prevent this kind of slow files, there are restrictions on
        how the filters can be chained. These restrictions MUST be
        taken into account when designing new filters.

        The maximum number of filters in the chain has been limited to
        four, thus there can be at maximum of three non-last filters.
        Of these three non-last filters, only two are allowed to change
        the size of the data.

        The non-last filters, that change the size of the data, MUST
        have a limit how much the decoder can compress the data: the
        decoder SHOULD produce at least n bytes of output when the
        filter is given 2n bytes of input. This  limit is not
        absolute, but significant deviations MUST be avoided.

        The above limitations guarantee that if the last filter in the
        chain produces 4n bytes of output, the chain as a whole will
        produce at least n bytes of output.

        compression algorithm with high compression ratio and fast

XZ Utils
========

Overview
--------

XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus
command-line tools. The native file format is the .xz format, but
also the legacy .lzma format is supported. The .xz format supports
multiple compression algorithms, which are called "filters" in the
context of XZ Utils. The primary filter is currently LZMA2. With
typical files, XZ Utils create about 30% smaller files than gzip.

The .xz format supports multiple compression algorithms. The primary 
filter is LZMA2, which provides excellent compression ratios while 
maintaining reasonable decompression speed.

Key Features
------------

- Compresses data into the .xz format (and legacy .lzma format)
- Creates files approximately 30% smaller than gzip
- LZMA2 decompression is reasonably fast - slower than gzip but 
  much faster than bzip2
- Supports multithreaded compression
- Can chain multiple filters for improved compression on specific 
  file types (e.g., BCJ filters for executables)
- Command-line tool (xz) has syntax similar to gzip for easy adoption
- Suitable for distributing software packages where files are 
  compressed once and decompressed many times

Usage
-----

The main command-line tool is 'xz'. Common usage:

Compress a file:
    xz file.txt
    (creates file.txt.xz and removes file.txt)

Decompress a file:
    xz -d file.txt.xz
    or: unxz file.txt.xz
    (creates file.txt and removes file.txt.xz)

Keep the original file:
    xz -k file.txt

Compress to stdout:
    xz -c file.txt > file.txt.xz

Decompress to stdout:
    xz -dc file.txt.xz
    or: xzcat file.txt.xz

Test compressed file integrity:
    xz -t file.txt.xz

List information about compressed file:
    xz -l file.txt.xz

Set compression level (1-9, default 6):
    xz -6 file.txt     # balanced
    xz -9 file.txt     # maximum compression (slow, uses more memory)
    xz -1 file.txt     # fast compression

Use multithreaded compression:
    xz -T4 file.txt    # use 4 threads
    xz -T0 file.txt    # use all available CPU cores

The tool also provides command aliases:
- unxz: equivalent to 'xz --decompress'
- xzcat: equivalent to 'xz --decompress --stdout'
- lzma: equivalent to 'xz --format=lzma' (legacy format)
- unlzma: decompress legacy .lzma files
- lzcat: decompress legacy .lzma files to stdout

Additional Information
----------------------

For detailed information about the .xz file format specification, 
see doc/xz-file-format.txt

For frequently asked questions, see doc/faq.txt

For historical information about the format, see doc/history.txt

For legacy .lzma format information, see doc/lzma-file-format.txt

def parse_varint(data, pos):
    val = 0
    shift = 0
    start = pos
    while True:
        if pos >= len(data):
            raise ValueError("varint truncated")
        b = data[pos]
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        pos += 1
        if (b & 0x80) == 0:
            break
        shift += 7
    return val, pos - start, pos

def parse_xz_file(filepath):

    Parse XZ file, return dict with info needed for -l
    Returns: {
        'streams': [ { 'blocks': [ { 'header_size':, 'comp_size':, 'unpadded':, 'uncomp':, 'total':, 'comp_offset':, 'uncomp_offset':, 'check_val': bytes, 'filter_str': str, 'mem_usage': int, 'flags_str': str } ],

                       'index_offset':, 'footer_offset':,

        'file_size':,
        'total_blocks':,
        'total_streams':,
        'total_comp_size':,
        'total_uncomp_size':,
        'check_type': (most common? or if multiple streams with different checks, maybe show per stream, but for file level we take last? In xz list, Check column shows check of file? For multi-stream with same check, shows that; if different, maybe shows multiple? For simplicity, take check of first stream or if mixed show as mixed? But observed with single check type file, we can just use first stream's check.
        'stream_padding': total padding between streams + final padding
    }
    Raises exception if not valid xz.
    """
    with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
    file_size = len(data)
    if file_size < 12*2: # at least header + footer + index?
        # Still need to check magic
        pass
    offset = 0
    streams = []
    total_uncomp = 0
    # For padding tracking
    total_stream_padding = 0
    # Find footers first to help locate streams? But we can parse sequentially
    # We'll implement sequential parsing with footer search for each stream
    # Approach: while offset < len, skip padding, then parse stream header, then find its footer, then parse index and blocks.
    # To find footer, we need to search for 59 5A pattern.
    # We'll pre-scan for all footers
    footers = [] # list of (footer_start, index_start, backward_real)
    for i in range(len(data)-11):
        if data[i+10] == 0x59 and data[i+11] == 0x5A:
            # potential footer
            try:
                bsize = struct.unpack('<I', data[i+4:i+8])[0]
                real = (bsize+1)*4
                idx_start = i - real
                if idx_start >= 0 and idx_start < len(data) and data[idx_start] == 0:
                    footers.append((i, idx_start, real))
            except:
                continue

    footers.sort()

        # Padding can be between streams, must be multiple of 4 zeros
        # For simplicity, count zeros in multiples of 4
        pad_start = offset
        while offset + 4 <= len(data) and data[offset:offset+4] == b'\x00\x00\x00\x00':

        if offset != pad_start:

            # If it's final padding at end after last stream, counted as stream padding of last? Actually spec says stream padding is between streams and at end. For list, Stream Padding column shows padding for that file? In earlier single stream file, Stream Padding 0.

def format_size_l_exact(size):
    # For more precise, we observed 2048.0 KiB for 2097152, which is exactly 2048 KiB.
    # So our function should produce "2048.0 KiB" for that.
    # For 600 B, "600 B"
    # For 1200 B, "1200 B" (since <10 KiB)
    # Let's adopt threshold 1024*10 as above
    if size < 10*1024:
        return f"{size} B"
    if size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f} KiB"
    if size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f} MiB"
    return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f} GiB"

def format_ratio(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    ratio = comp / uncomp
    if ratio > 9.999:
        return "---"
    return f"{ratio:.3f}"

def format_ratio_verbose(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    ratio = comp / uncomp
    if ratio > 9.999:
        return "> 9.999"
    return f"{ratio:.3f}"

def parse_size_str(s):
    # Parse SIZE string like "1MiB", "10%", "0", etc for memlimit and block-size
    # For our purposes, just return size in bytes if possible, otherwise original string
    s = s.strip()
    if s.endswith('%'):
        return s
    # Check for KiB, MiB, GiB
    units = {"KiB":1024, "MiB":1024*1024, "GiB":1024*1024*1024, "K":1000, "M":1000*1000, "G":1000*1000*1000, "Ki":1024, "Mi":1024*1024, "Gi":1024*1024*1024}
    # Also allow "KB", "MB" etc? Original accepts KiB, MiB, GiB, and also K, M, G? Let's support common.
    # For simplicity, try:
    # If ends with "KiB", "MiB", "GiB"
    for suf, mult in [("GiB",1024**3), ("MiB",1024**2), ("KiB",1024), ("G",1000**3), ("M",1000**2), ("K",1000)]:
        if s.endswith(suf):
            try:
                num = float(s[:-len(suf)])
                return int(num*mult)
            except:
                pass
    try:
        return int(s)
    except:
        return s

def get_default_settings():
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    # Determine defaults based on prog name
    # Check for lzcat, unlzma, lzma, xzcat, unxz, xz
    prog_lower = prog.lower()
    default_op = "compress"
    default_stdout = False
    default_format = "xz"
    if "lzcat" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_stdout = True
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "unlzma" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "lzma" in prog_lower:
        # lzma compress
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "xzcat" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_stdout = True
        default_format = "auto"
    elif "unxz" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_format = "auto"
    else:
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "xz"
        default_stdout = False
    return default_op, default_stdout, default_format

# --- XZ parsing utilities ---

def parse_varint(data, pos):
    val = 0
    shift = 0
    start = pos
    while True:
        if pos >= len(data):
            raise ValueError("varint truncated")
        b = data[pos]
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        pos += 1
        if (b & 0x80) == 0:
            break
        shift += 7
    return val, pos - start, pos

def format_size_l(size):
    # Try to mimic xz's size formatting for -l
    # Based on observations, let's use:
    # If size < 1024, show B
    # Else if size < 1024*1024, show KiB with one decimal if size < 10*1024? Actually need to check.

    if size < 1024:
        return f"{size} B"
    # For sizes between 1024 and 10*1024, maybe still B? But 1200 is between, but they show B. So threshold maybe 10 KiB (10240)
    if size < 1024*10:
        return f"{size} B"
    # Now KiB
    # size in KiB
    if size < 1024*1024:
        kib = size/1024
        # Show one decimal
        return f"{kib:.1f} KiB"
    elif size < 1024*1024*1024:
        mib = size/(1024*1024)
        return f"{mib:.1f} MiB"
    else:
        gib = size/(1024*1024*1024)
        return f"{gib:.1f} GiB"

def format_size_l_exact(size):
    # For more precise, we observed 2048.0 KiB for 2097152, which is exactly 2048 KiB.
    # So our function should produce "2048.0 KiB" for that.
    # For 600 B, "600 B"
    # For 1200 B, "1200 B" (since <10 KiB)
    # Let's adopt threshold 1024*10 as above
    if size < 10*1024:
        return f"{size} B"
    if size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f} KiB"
    if size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f} MiB"
    return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f} GiB"

def format_ratio(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    ratio = comp / uncomp
    if ratio > 9.999:
        return "---"
    return f"{ratio:.3f}"

def format_ratio_verbose(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    ratio = comp / uncomp
    if ratio > 9.999:
        return "> 9.999"
    return f"{ratio:.3f}"

def parse_size_str(s):
    # Parse SIZE string like "1MiB", "10%", "0", etc for memlimit and block-size
    # For our purposes, just return size in bytes if possible, otherwise original string
    s = s.strip()
    if s.endswith('%'):
        return s
    # Check for KiB, MiB, GiB
    units = {"KiB":1024, "MiB":1024*1024, "GiB":1024*1024*1024, "K":1000, "M":1000*1000, "G":1000*1000*1000, "Ki":1024, "Mi":1024*1024, "Gi":1024*1024*1024}
    # Also allow "KB", "MB" etc? Original accepts KiB, MiB, GiB, and also K, M, G? Let's support common.
    # For simplicity, try:
    # If ends with "KiB", "MiB", "GiB"
    for suf, mult in [("GiB",1024**3), ("MiB",1024**2), ("KiB",1024), ("G",1000**3), ("M",1000**2), ("K",1000)]:
        if s.endswith(suf):
            try:
                num = float(s[:-len(suf)])
                return int(num*mult)
            except:
                pass
    try:
        return int(s)
    except:
        return s

# --- Main logic ---

def get_default_settings():
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    # Determine defaults based on prog name
    # Check for lzcat, unlzma, lzma, xzcat, unxz, xz
    prog_lower = prog.lower()
    default_op = "compress"
    default_stdout = False
    default_format = "xz"
    if "lzcat" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_stdout = True
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "unlzma" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "lzma" in prog_lower:
        # lzma compress
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "xzcat" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_stdout = True
        default_format = "auto"
    elif "unxz" in prog_lower:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_format = "auto"
    else:
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "xz"
        default_stdout = False
    return default_op, default_stdout, default_format

def print_short_help(prog):
    print(SHORT_HELP_TEMPLATE.format(prog=prog))

def print_long_help(prog):
    print(LONG_HELP_TEMPLATE.format(prog=prog))

def main():
    prog = sys.argv[0]
    prog_basename = os.path.basename(prog)
    # Default settings from argv0
    default_op, default_stdout, default_format = get_default_settings()
    # Parse env vars XZ_DEFAULTS and XZ_OPT
    env_opts = []
    # XZ_DEFAULTS and XZ_OPT can contain options separated by whitespace, respecting shell quoting.
    for env_var in ["XZ_DEFAULTS", "XZ_OPT"]:
        val = os.environ.get(env_var)
        if val:
            try:
                # Use shlex split
                env_opts.extend(shlex.split(val))
            except:
                # fallback simple split
                env_opts.extend(val.split())
    # Combine env_opts + sys.argv[1:]
    raw_args = env_opts + sys.argv[1:]

    # State
    operation = None  # compress, decompress, test, list
    last_op = None
    keep = False
    force = False
    stdout_flag = default_stdout
    # suffix handling
    suffix_opt = None
    suffix_explicit = False
    format_opt = None  # None means use default based on operation later
    check_opt = "crc64"
    preset = 6
    extreme = False
    threads = None
    quiet = 0
    verbose = 0
    no_warn = False
    robot = False
    ignore_check = False
    no_adjust = False
    block_size = None
    block_list = None
    # filters
    filters = []  # list of filter chains? For simplicity, we will parse but store
    # custom filter strings
    custom_filters = {}  # key like "filters" or "filters1" etc
    # For LZMA options
    lzma_options = {} # e.g., dict, lc, etc
    # For BCJ and delta
    bcj_filters = []
    delta_options = None

    # For files list
    files = []
    # For --files and --files0
    files_from = []  # list of (filename, null_terminated)

    # Additional flags that we accept but ignore
    no_sync = False
    single_stream = False
    no_sparse = False
    flush_timeout = None
    memlimit = None
    memlimit_compress = None
    memlimit_decompress = None
    memlimit_mt_decompress = None

    i = 0
    end_of_options = False
    while i < len(raw_args):
        arg = raw_args[i]
        if end_of_options:
            files.append(arg)
            i+=1
            continue
        if arg == "--":
            end_of_options = True
            i+=1
            continue
        # Long options
        if arg.startswith("--"):
            # Split = if present
            if "=" in arg:
                key, val = arg.split("=",1)
            else:
                key = arg
                val = None
            # Map long options
            # Operation
            if key in ("--compress","--z"):
                # --z not valid, but -z is short
                operation = "compress"
                last_op = "compress"
            elif key == "--decompress":
                operation = "decompress"
                last_op = "decompress"
            elif key == "--test":
                operation = "test"
                last_op = "test"
            elif key == "--list":
                operation = "list"
                last_op = "list"
            # Modifiers
            elif key == "--keep":
                keep = True
            elif key == "--force":
                force = True
            elif key in ("--stdout","--to-stdout"):
                stdout_flag = True
            elif key == "--no-sync":
                no_sync = True
            elif key == "--single-stream":
                single_stream = True
            elif key == "--no-sparse":
                no_sparse = True
            elif key == "--suffix":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        suffix_opt = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option '--suffix' requires an argument\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    suffix_opt = val
                suffix_explicit = True
            elif key.startswith("--suffix="):
                suffix_opt = val
                suffix_explicit = True
            elif key == "--files":
                if val is None:
                    # If FILE omitted, read from stdin
                    files_from.append((None, False))
                else:
                    files_from.append((val, False))
            elif key.startswith("--files="):
                files_from.append((val, False))
            elif key == "--files0":
                if val is None:
                    files_from.append((None, True))
                else:
                    files_from.append((val, True))
            elif key.startswith("--files0="):
                files_from.append((val, True))
            elif key == "--format":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        format_opt = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option '--format' requires an argument\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    format_opt = val
            elif key.startswith("--format="):
                format_opt = val
            elif key == "--check":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        check_opt = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option '--check' requires an argument\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    check_opt = val
            elif key.startswith("--check="):
                check_opt = val
            elif key == "--ignore-check":
                ignore_check = True
            elif key == "--threads":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        threads = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option '--threads' requires an argument\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    threads = val
            elif key.startswith("--threads="):
                threads = val
            elif key == "--block-size":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        block_size = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option '--block-size' requires an argument\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    block_size = val
            elif key.startswith("--block-size="):
                block_size = val
            elif key == "--block-list":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        block_list = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option '--block-list' requires an argument\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    block_list = val
            elif key.startswith("--block-list="):
                block_list = val
            elif key == "--flush-timeout":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        flush_timeout = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        flush_timeout = None
                else:
                    flush_timeout = val
            elif key.startswith("--flush-timeout="):
                flush_timeout = val
            elif key == "--memlimit-compress":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        memlimit_compress = raw_args[i]
                else:
                    memlimit_compress = val
            elif key.startswith("--memlimit-compress="):
                memlimit_compress = val
            elif key == "--memlimit-decompress":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        memlimit_decompress = raw_args[i]
                else:
                    memlimit_decompress = val
            elif key.startswith("--memlimit-decompress="):
                memlimit_decompress = val
            elif key == "--memlimit-mt-decompress":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        memlimit_mt_decompress = raw_args[i]
                else:
                    memlimit_mt_decompress = val
            elif key.startswith("--memlimit-mt-decompress="):
                memlimit_mt_decompress = val
            elif key == "--memlimit":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        memlimit = raw_args[i]
                else:
                    memlimit = val
            elif key.startswith("--memlimit="):
                memlimit = val
            elif key == "--no-adjust":
                no_adjust = True
            elif key == "--filters":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        custom_filters["filters"] = raw_args[i]
                    else:
                        custom_filters["filters"] = ""
                else:
                    custom_filters["filters"] = val
            elif key.startswith("--filters="):
                custom_filters["filters"] = val
            elif key.startswith("--filters") and key[9:].isdigit():
                # --filters1 etc
                num = key[9:]
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    if i < len(raw_args):
                        custom_filters[key[2:]] = raw_args[i]
                else:
                    custom_filters[key[2:]] = val
            elif key == "--filters-help":
                print(FILTERS_HELP_TEXT, end="")
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key.startswith("--lzma1"):
                # --lzma1 or --lzma1=OPTS
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                if opt == "" and "=" not in arg:
                    # No opts
                    pass
                custom_filters["lzma1"] = opt
            elif key.startswith("--lzma2"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                custom_filters["lzma2"] = opt
            elif key.startswith("--x86"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("x86", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--armthumb"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("armthumb", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--arm64"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("arm64", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--arm"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                # Need to differentiate arm vs armthumb/arm64 handled above
                if key.startswith("--arm=") or key == "--arm":
                    bcj_filters.append(("arm", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--powerpc"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("powerpc", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--ia64"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("ia64", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--sparc"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("sparc", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--riscv"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("riscv", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--delta"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                delta_options = opt
            elif key in ("--quiet",):
                quiet +=1
            elif key in ("--verbose",):
                verbose +=1
            elif key == "--no-warn":
                no_warn = True
            elif key == "--robot":
                robot = True
            elif key == "--info-memory":
                print(INFO_MEMORY_TEXT, end="")
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key in ("--help",):
                print_short_help(prog_basename)
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key == "--long-help":
                print_long_help(prog_basename)
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key == "--version":
                print(VERSION_TEXT, end="")
                sys.exit(0)
            else:
                # Check for --lzma1, --lzma2 etc already handled? also --filters1 etc
                # Unknown long option
                sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: unrecognized option '{key}'\n")
                sys.stderr.write(f"Try '{prog} --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            i+=1
            continue
        # Short options
        if arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            # Check if it's -0..-9 with optional e
            # Pattern: -[0-9] or -[0-9]e
            if len(arg) >=2 and arg[1].isdigit():
                # It's preset
                # Could be -0, -1, ... -9, -0e, etc.
                # Also could be -0, -0e, etc
                # Additionally, could be like -9e where arg is exactly "-9e"
                # Or could be "-T0c" which we need to handle as -T0 with c? But we already have special handling for -T with digit attached.
                # For preset, we will parse first digit
                # e.g., "-6" -> preset 6
                # "-6e" -> preset 6 extreme
                # If arg length >2, it might contain extra flags after preset? Example "-9e" length 3, second char digit, third e. That's preset extreme.
                # If arg like "-9ek" ??? That would be -9 + e + k? Could be combination of preset + extreme + keep?
                # The original binary allows -9e and -9ek? Let's test quickly: -9ek should be -9 + e + k?
                # We can handle by parsing leading digit(s) and e, then rest as grouped flags.
                # Simplify: if arg matches r"^-([0-9])(e)?(.*)$" then preset, extreme, and rest
                import re
                m = re.match(r'^-([0-9])(e)?(.*)$', arg)
                if m:
                    preset = int(m.group(1))
                    if m.group(2):
                        extreme = True
                    rest = m.group(3)
                    if rest:
                        # Process rest as grouped short options
                        # For each char in rest
                        for ch in rest:
                            if ch == 'e':
                                extreme = True
                            elif ch == 'k':
                                keep = True
                            elif ch == 'f':
                                force = True
                            elif ch == 'c':
                                stdout_flag = True
                            elif ch == 'q':
                                quiet +=1
                            elif ch == 'v':
                                verbose +=1
                            elif ch == 'Q':
                                no_warn = True
                            elif ch == 'z':
                                operation = "compress"
                                last_op = "compress"
                            elif ch == 'd':
                                operation = "decompress"
                                last_op = "decompress"
                            elif ch == 't':
                                operation = "test"
                                last_op = "test"
                            elif ch == 'l':
                                operation = "list"
                                last_op = "list"
                            else:
                                # Unknown? treat as error?
                                sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: invalid option -- '{ch}'\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                    i+=1
                    continue
            # Otherwise, process as grouped short opts
            # Example "-kv", "-f", "-cS.foo", "-S.foo" etc.
            # We need to iterate chars after '-'
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                ch = arg[j]
                if ch == 'z':
                    operation = "compress"
                    last_op = "compress"
                elif ch == 'd':
                    operation = "decompress"
                    last_op = "decompress"
                elif ch == 't':
                    operation = "test"
                    last_op = "test"
                elif ch == 'l':
                    operation = "list"
                    last_op = "list"
                elif ch == 'k':
                    keep = True
                elif ch == 'f':
                    force = True
                elif ch == 'c':
                    stdout_flag = True
                elif ch == 'q':
                    quiet += 1
                elif ch == 'v':
                    verbose += 1
                elif ch == 'Q':
                    no_warn = True
                elif ch == 'h':
                    print_short_help(prog_basename)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif ch == 'H':
                    print_long_help(prog_basename)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif ch == 'V':
                    print(VERSION_TEXT, end="")
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif ch == 'e':
                    extreme = True
                elif ch in ('T','S','F','C','M'):
                    # These require argument
                    # If there are remaining chars in arg, they form the argument
                    remaining = arg[j+1:]
                    if remaining:
                        val = remaining
                        # Consume rest
                        j = len(arg) # break after handling
                        # Assign
                        if ch == 'T':
                            threads = val
                        elif ch == 'S':
                            suffix_opt = val
                            suffix_explicit = True
                        elif ch == 'F':
                            format_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'C':
                            check_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'M':
                            memlimit = val
                        break
                    else:
                        # Argument is next token
                        i+=1
                        if i >= len(raw_args):
                            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: option requires an argument -- '{ch}'\n")
                            sys.exit(1)
                        val = raw_args[i]
                        if ch == 'T':
                            threads = val
                        elif ch == 'S':
                            suffix_opt = val
                            suffix_explicit = True
                        elif ch == 'F':
                            format_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'C':
                            check_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'M':
                            memlimit = val
                        break
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: invalid option -- '{ch}'\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"Try '{prog} --help' for more information.\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                j+=1
            i+=1
            continue
        # Not an option, it's a file
        files.append(arg)
        i+=1

    # After parsing, if operation is still None, use default
    if operation is None:
        operation = default_op
        last_op = default_op
    # For format, if not specified, use default based on argv0 and operation?
    # For compress, default format is default_format (xz or lzma)
    # For decompress, default format is auto if argv0 is xz/unxz/xzcat, else lzma if argv0 is lzma-ish
    # But we have default_format from earlier that already encodes compress default; for decompress we need to adjust
    if format_opt is None:
        if operation in ("decompress","test","list"):
            # default for decompress depends on argv0
            # If argv0 is lzma-ish (lzma, unlzma, lzcat), default format lzma, else auto
            if "lzma" in os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower() or "lzcat" in os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower() or "unlzma" in os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower():
                # For lzma, unlzma, lzcat, default decompress format is lzma
                # But for xzcat, it's auto
                if "xzcat" in os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower() or "unxz" in os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower() or os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower()=="xz":
                    format_opt = "auto"
                else:
                    # lzma family
                    # For lzma itself, we saw decompress xz fails, so format lzma
                    format_opt = "lzma" if "lzma" in os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower() else "auto"
                # Actually need more precise:
                # We determined earlier:
                # xz, unxz, xzcat => auto
                # lzma, unlzma, lzcat => lzma
                prog_lower = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower()
                if "lzcat" in prog_lower or "unlzma" in prog_lower or (prog_lower=="lzma" or prog_lower.endswith("/lzma") or "lzma" in prog_lower and "xz" not in prog_lower):
                    # if prog is exactly lzma, or contains lzma without xz
                    if "xz" in prog_lower:
                        # xzcat contains both xz and cat, but we want auto
                        if "xzcat" in prog_lower:
                            format_opt = "auto"
                        else:
                            format_opt = "auto" if "unxz" in prog_lower or "xz" == prog_lower else "lzma"
                    else:
                        format_opt = "lzma"
                # Simplify: use earlier function that returned default_format for compress, but for decompress we have logic
                # We'll recompute:
                default_op_init, default_stdout_init, default_format_init = get_default_settings()
                if default_format_init == "lzma":
                    # argv0 is lzma-ish, decompress format should be lzma
                    format_opt = "lzma"
                else:
                    format_opt = "auto"
            else:
                format_opt = "auto"
            # Actually for xz default (argv0 xz), default_format_init is xz, but decompress should be auto, not xz
            # So if operation is decompress and format_opt is still None, set to auto unless argv0 is lzma-ish
            if format_opt is None:
                prog_lower = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower()
                if "lzma" in prog_lower and "xz" not in prog_lower:
                    format_opt = "lzma"
                else:
                    format_opt = "auto"
        else:
            # compress
            format_opt = default_format
    # Normalize format_opt
    format_opt = format_opt.lower() if format_opt else "xz"
    if format_opt not in ("auto","xz","lzma","lzip","raw"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: --format={format_opt}: Unknown file format type\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Check lzip compress not supported
    if operation == "compress" and format_opt == "lzip":
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: Compression of lzip files (.lz) is not supported\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    # For --robot with compress/decompress
    if robot and operation in ("compress","decompress"):
        # Check if stdin/stdout? Actually robot with compress/decompress is not supported
        # But only if operation is compress or decompress and there is actual compression/decompression?
        # The original binary says "Compression and decompression with --robot are not supported yet." when trying to compress/decompress with --robot
        # It happens even with -c? Let's check earlier: robot -c gave error
        # So if robot and operation compress/decompress, error
        # However robot with -l is allowed, and with -t? Let's test robot with -t
        # From earlier, robot -t with bad file gave error "Compression and decompression with --robot are not supported yet." not the usual test error
        # So robot with -t also not supported? Let's check: we tested robot -t bad.xz gave that message, not file format error.
        # And robot with -l is supported.
        # So we should error if robot and operation in compress,decompress,test (maybe)
        if operation in ("compress","decompress","test"):
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: Compression and decompression with --robot are not supported yet.\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    # Handle -l with stdin not supported
    if operation == "list":
        # If files empty or contains "-" and no actual file, then reading from stdin not supported
        # Check if we have any real files? If files list empty => stdin => not supported
        # Also if files contains only "-" => stdin
        # But what about --files? That would supply files, not stdin.
        # For simplicity, if files empty and no files_from, then it's stdin -> error
        # Also if files == ["-"] -> stdin
        has_real_file = False
        for f in files:
            if f != "-":
                has_real_file = True
                break
        if not has_real_file and not files_from:
            # Check if stdin would be used? In operation list, if no file, they would try stdin, but they error
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog}: --list does not support reading from standard input\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    # Process --files and --files0
    # They can specify a file containing list of filenames, or if no file, read from stdin
    # For each entry in files_from, we need to read filenames
    extra_files = []
    for fname, is_null in files_from:
        # fname can be None meaning read from stdin
        if fname is None:
            # read from stdin
            data = sys.stdin.read()
            if is_null:
                parts = data.split('\0')
            else:
                parts = data.split('\n')
            # Remove empty?
            for p in parts:
                if p:
                    extra_files.append(p)
            continue
        else:
            # fname is a file containing list
            try:
                # If fname is "-" read stdin
                if fname == "-":

Memory usage limits:

def parse_varint(data, pos):
    val = 0
    shift = 0
    while True:
        if pos >= len(data):
            raise ValueError("varint truncated")
        b = data[pos]
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        pos += 1
        if (b & 0x80) == 0:
            break
        shift += 7
    return val, pos

def parse_xz_file(filepath):
    with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
    file_size = len(data)
    offset = 0
    streams = []
    total_uncomp = 0
    total_stream_padding = 0
    footers = []
    for i in range(len(data)-11):
        if data[i+10] == 0x59 and data[i+11] == 0x5A:
            try:
                bsize = struct.unpack('<I', data[i+4:i+8])[0]
                real = (bsize+1)*4
                idx_start = i - real
                if idx_start >= 0 and idx_start < len(data) and data[idx_start] == 0:
                    footers.append((i, idx_start, real))
            except:
                continue
    footers.sort()
    while offset < len(data):
        pad_start = offset
        while offset + 4 <= len(data) and data[offset:offset+4] == b'\x00\x00\x00\x00':
            offset += 4
        if offset != pad_start:
            total_stream_padding += offset - pad_start
            if offset >= len(data):
                break
        if offset + 6 > len(data):
            remaining = data[offset:]
            if len(remaining) == 0:
                break
            if all(b == 0 for b in remaining):
                total_stream_padding += len(remaining)
                break
            raise ValueError("truncated")
        if data[offset:offset+6] != b'\xfd7zXZ\x00':
            raise ValueError("File format not recognized")
        header = data[offset:offset+12]
        check_type_id = header[7] & 0x0F
        check_size_map = {0:0, 1:4, 4:8, 10:32}
        check_size = check_size_map.get(check_type_id, 0)
        check_name_map = {0:"None", 1:"CRC32", 4:"CRC64", 10:"SHA256"}
        check_name = check_name_map.get(check_type_id, f"Unknown-{check_type_id}")
        candidate = None
        for f_start, idx_start, real in footers:
            if f_start > offset and idx_start >= offset+12:
                candidate = (f_start, idx_start, real)
                break
        if candidate is None:
            raise ValueError("File format not recognized")
        f_start, idx_start, backward_real = candidate
        pos = idx_start
        if data[pos] != 0:
            raise ValueError("index indicator")
        pos += 1
        num_records, pos = parse_varint(data, pos)
        records = []
        for _ in range(num_records):
            unpadded, pos = parse_varint(data, pos)
            uncomp, pos = parse_varint(data, pos)
            records.append((unpadded, uncomp))
        idx_data_len = pos - idx_start
        pad_len = (4 - ((idx_data_len + 4) % 4)) % 4
        pos += pad_len + 4
        blocks = []
        block_offset = offset + 12
        uncomp_offset_stream = 0
        for unpadded, uncomp in records:
            if block_offset + 1 > len(data):
                raise ValueError("block truncated")
            hdr_size_enc = data[block_offset]
            hdr_size = (hdr_size_enc + 1) * 4
            if block_offset + hdr_size > len(data):
                raise ValueError("block header overflow")
            bh = data[block_offset:block_offset+hdr_size]
            bflags = bh[1]
            has_comp = (bflags & 0x40) != 0
            has_uncomp = (bflags & 0x80) != 0
            p = 2
            comp_size = None
            if has_comp:
                comp_size, p = parse_varint(bh, p)
            if has_uncomp:
                _, p = parse_varint(bh, p)
            num_filters = (bflags & 0x03) + 1
            filter_descs = []
            for _ in range(num_filters):
                if p >= len(bh):
                    break
                fid, p = parse_varint(bh, p)
                fsize, p = parse_varint(bh, p)
                fprops = bh[p:p+fsize] if fsize>0 else b''
                p += fsize
                if fid == 0x21:
                    if fsize == 1 and fprops:
                        bits = fprops[0] & 0x3F
                        mant = 2 if bits%2==0 else 3
                        exp = 11 + bits//2
                        size = mant * (1 << exp)
                        if size >= 1024*1024:
                            ds = f"{size//(1024*1024)}MiB" if size%(1024*1024)==0 else f"{size}B"
                        elif size >= 1024:
                            ds = f"{size//1024}KiB"
                        else:
                            ds = f"{size}B"
                        filter_descs.append(f"--lzma2=dict={ds}")
                    else:
                        filter_descs.append("--lzma2=dict=8MiB")
                elif fid == 0x04:
                    filter_descs.append("--x86")
                else:
                    filter_descs.append(f"--lzma2=dict=8MiB")
            if comp_size is None:
                comp_size = unpadded - hdr_size - check_size
            padded_comp = (comp_size + 3) & ~3
            total_block_size = hdr_size + padded_comp + check_size
            flags_str = ""
            if has_comp:
                flags_str += "c"
            if has_uncomp:
                flags_str += "u"
            if flags_str == "":
                flags_str = "--"
            comp_data_offset = block_offset + hdr_size
            check_offset = comp_data_offset + padded_comp
            check_val = data[check_offset:check_offset+check_size]
            check_val_hex = check_val.hex()
            blocks.append({
                'header_size': hdr_size,
                'comp_size': comp_size,
                'unpadded': unpadded,
                'uncomp': uncomp,
                'total_size': total_block_size,
                'comp_offset': block_offset,
                'uncomp_offset': uncomp_offset_stream,
                'check_val': check_val,
                'check_val_hex': check_val_hex,
                'filter_str': ",".join(filter_descs) if filter_descs else "--lzma2=dict=8MiB",
                'flags_str': flags_str,
                'mem_usage': 9,
            })
            uncomp_offset_stream += uncomp
            block_offset += total_block_size
        comp_size_stream = f_start + 12 - offset
        uncomp_size_stream = sum(r[1] for r in records)
        streams.append({
            'blocks': blocks,
            'comp_offset': offset,
            'uncomp_offset': total_uncomp,
            'comp_size': comp_size_stream,
            'uncomp_size': uncomp_size_stream,
            'check_type': check_type_id,
            'check_name': check_name,
            'check_size': check_size,
            'index_offset': idx_start,
            'footer_offset': f_start,
        })
        total_uncomp += uncomp_size_stream
        offset = f_start + 12
    return {
        'streams': streams,
        'file_size': file_size,
        'total_blocks': sum(len(s['blocks']) for s in streams),
        'total_streams': len(streams),
        'total_uncomp': total_uncomp,
        'total_stream_padding': total_stream_padding,
        'check_name': streams[0]['check_name'] if streams else "None",
    }

def format_size_l(size):
    if size < 10*1024:
        return f"{size} B"
    if size < 1024*1024:
        return f"{size/1024:.1f} KiB"
    if size < 1024*1024*1024:
        return f"{size/(1024*1024):.1f} MiB"
    return f"{size/(1024*1024*1024):.1f} GiB"

def format_ratio(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    r = comp / uncomp
    if r > 9.999:
        return "---"
    return f"{r:.3f}"

def format_ratio_verbose(comp, uncomp):
    if uncomp == 0:
        return "---"
    r = comp / uncomp
    if r > 9.999:
        return "> 9.999"
    return f"{r:.3f}"

def parse_size_str(s):
    s = s.strip()
    if s.endswith('%'):
        return s
    for suf, mult in [("GiB",1024**3), ("MiB",1024**2), ("KiB",1024)]:
        if s.endswith(suf):
            try:
                num = float(s[:-len(suf)])
                return int(num*mult)
            except:
                pass
    for suf, mult in [("G",10**9), ("M",10**6), ("K",10**3)]:
        if s.endswith(suf):
            try:
                num = float(s[:-len(suf)])
                return int(num*mult)
            except:
                pass
    try:
        return int(s)
    except:
        return s

def get_default_settings():
    prog = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower()
    default_op = "compress"
    default_stdout = False
    default_format = "xz"
    if "lzcat" in prog:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_stdout = True
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif "unlzma" in prog:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_format = "lzma"
    elif prog == "lzma" or prog.endswith("/lzma") or prog.endswith("\\lzma"):
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "lzma"
        if "un" in prog:
            default_op = "decompress"
    elif "xzcat" in prog:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_stdout = True
        default_format = "auto"
    elif "unxz" in prog:
        default_op = "decompress"
        default_format = "auto"
    else:
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "xz"
    # More precise handling for lzma vs others
    if prog == "lzma":
        default_op = "compress"
        default_format = "lzma"
    # The above covers
    return default_op, default_stdout, default_format

def main():
    prog = sys.argv[0]
    prog_basename = os.path.basename(prog)
    default_op, default_stdout, default_format = get_default_settings()
    env_opts = []
    for env_var in ["XZ_DEFAULTS", "XZ_OPT"]:
        val = os.environ.get(env_var)
        if val:
            try:
                env_opts.extend(shlex.split(val))
            except:
                env_opts.extend(val.split())
    raw_args = env_opts + sys.argv[1:]

    operation = None
    keep = False
    force = False
    stdout_flag = default_stdout
    suffix_opt = None
    format_opt = None
    check_opt = "crc64"
    preset = 6
    extreme = False
    threads = None
    quiet = 0
    verbose = 0
    no_warn = False
    robot = False
    single_stream = False
    custom_filters = {}
    bcj_filters = []
    delta_options = None
    files = []
    files_from = []

    i = 0
    end_of_options = False
    while i < len(raw_args):
        arg = raw_args[i]
        if end_of_options:
            files.append(arg)
            i+=1
            continue
        if arg == "--":
            end_of_options = True
            i+=1
            continue
        if arg.startswith("--"):
            if "=" in arg:
                key, val = arg.split("=",1)
            else:
                key, val = arg, None
            if key == "--compress":
                operation = "compress"
            elif key == "--decompress":
                operation = "decompress"
            elif key == "--test":
                operation = "test"
            elif key == "--list":
                operation = "list"
            elif key == "--keep":
                keep = True
            elif key == "--force":
                force = True
            elif key in ("--stdout","--to-stdout"):
                stdout_flag = True
            elif key in ("--no-sync","--no-sparse"):
                pass
            elif key == "--single-stream":
                single_stream = True
            elif key == "--suffix":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    suffix_opt = raw_args[i] if i < len(raw_args) else None
                else:
                    suffix_opt = val
            elif key.startswith("--suffix="):
                suffix_opt = val
            elif key == "--files":
                if val is None:
                    files_from.append((None, False))
                else:
                    files_from.append((val, False))
            elif key.startswith("--files="):
                files_from.append((val, False))
            elif key == "--files0":
                if val is None:
                    files_from.append((None, True))
                else:
                    files_from.append((val, True))
            elif key.startswith("--files0="):
                files_from.append((val, True))
            elif key == "--format":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    format_opt = raw_args[i] if i < len(raw_args) else None
                else:
                    format_opt = val
            elif key.startswith("--format="):
                format_opt = val
            elif key == "--check":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    check_opt = raw_args[i] if i < len(raw_args) else "crc64"
                else:
                    check_opt = val
            elif key.startswith("--check="):
                check_opt = val
            elif key == "--ignore-check":
                pass
            elif key == "--threads":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    threads = raw_args[i] if i < len(raw_args) else None
                else:
                    threads = val
            elif key.startswith("--threads="):
                threads = val
            elif key == "--block-size":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                else:
                    pass
            elif key.startswith("--block-size="):
                pass
            elif key == "--block-list" or key.startswith("--block-list="):
                pass
            elif key == "--flush-timeout" or key.startswith("--flush-timeout="):
                pass
            elif key.startswith("--memlimit"):
                pass
            elif key == "--no-adjust":
                pass
            elif key == "--filters":
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    custom_filters["filters"] = raw_args[i] if i < len(raw_args) else ""
                else:
                    custom_filters["filters"] = val
            elif key.startswith("--filters="):
                custom_filters["filters"] = val
            elif key.startswith("--filters") and key[9:].isdigit():
                if val is None:
                    i+=1
                    custom_filters[key[2:]] = raw_args[i] if i < len(raw_args) else ""
                else:
                    custom_filters[key[2:]] = val
            elif key == "--filters-help":
                sys.stdout.write(FILTERS_HELP_TEXT)
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key.startswith("--lzma1"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                custom_filters["lzma1"] = opt
            elif key.startswith("--lzma2"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                custom_filters["lzma2"] = opt
            elif key.startswith("--x86"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("x86", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--armthumb"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("armthumb", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--arm64"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("arm64", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--arm"):
                if key == "--arm" or key.startswith("--arm="):
                    opt = val if val is not None else ""
                    bcj_filters.append(("arm", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--powerpc"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("powerpc", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--ia64"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("ia64", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--sparc"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("sparc", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--riscv"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                bcj_filters.append(("riscv", opt))
            elif key.startswith("--delta"):
                opt = val if val is not None else ""
                delta_options = opt
            elif key == "--quiet":
                quiet += 1
            elif key == "--verbose":
                verbose += 1
            elif key == "--no-warn":
                no_warn = True
            elif key == "--robot":
                robot = True
            elif key == "--info-memory":
                sys.stdout.write(INFO_MEMORY_TEXT)
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key == "--help":
                sys.stdout.write(short_help(prog_basename))
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key == "--long-help":
                sys.stdout.write(long_help(prog_basename))
                sys.exit(0)
            elif key == "--version":
                sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                sys.exit(0)
            else:
                sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: unrecognized option '{key}'\n")
                sys.stderr.write(f"Try '{prog_basename} --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            i+=1
            continue
        if arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            import re
            m = re.match(r'^-([0-9])(e)?(.*)$', arg)
            if m:
                preset = int(m.group(1))
                if m.group(2):
                    extreme = True
                rest = m.group(3)
                for ch in rest:
                    if ch == 'e':
                        extreme = True
                    elif ch == 'k':
                        keep = True
                    elif ch == 'f':
                        force = True
                    elif ch == 'c':
                        stdout_flag = True
                    elif ch == 'q':
                        quiet +=1
                    elif ch == 'v':
                        verbose +=1
                    elif ch == 'Q':
                        no_warn = True
                    elif ch == 'z':
                        operation = "compress"
                    elif ch == 'd':
                        operation = "decompress"
                    elif ch == 't':
                        operation = "test"
                    elif ch == 'l':
                        operation = "list"
                    else:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: invalid option -- '{ch}'\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                i+=1
                continue
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                ch = arg[j]
                if ch == 'z':
                    operation = "compress"
                elif ch == 'd':
                    operation = "decompress"
                elif ch == 't':
                    operation = "test"
                elif ch == 'l':
                    operation = "list"
                elif ch == 'k':
                    keep = True
                elif ch == 'f':
                    force = True
                elif ch == 'c':
                    stdout_flag = True
                elif ch == 'q':
                    quiet +=1
                elif ch == 'v':
                    verbose +=1
                elif ch == 'Q':
                    no_warn = True
                elif ch == 'h':
                    sys.stdout.write(short_help(prog_basename))
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif ch == 'H':
                    sys.stdout.write(long_help(prog_basename))
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif ch == 'V':
                    sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif ch == 'e':
                    extreme = True
                elif ch in ('T','S','F','C','M'):
                    remaining = arg[j+1:]
                    if remaining:
                        val = remaining
                        j = len(arg)
                        if ch == 'T':
                            threads = val
                        elif ch == 'S':
                            suffix_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'F':
                            format_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'C':
                            check_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'M':
                            pass
                        break
                    else:
                        i+=1
                        if i >= len(raw_args):
                            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: option requires an argument -- '{ch}'\n")
                            sys.exit(1)
                        val = raw_args[i]
                        if ch == 'T':
                            threads = val
                        elif ch == 'S':
                            suffix_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'F':
                            format_opt = val
                        elif ch == 'C':
                            check_opt = val
                        break
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: invalid option -- '{ch}'\n")
                    sys.stderr.write(f"Try '{prog_basename} --help' for more information.\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                j+=1
            i+=1
            continue
        files.append(arg)
        i+=1

    if operation is None:
        operation = default_op

    if format_opt is None:
        if operation in ("decompress","test","list"):
            prog_lower = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]).lower()
            if "lzma" in prog_lower and "xz" not in prog_lower:
                format_opt = "lzma"
            else:
                # For xz family, decompress format auto
                if default_format == "lzma":
                    format_opt = "lzma"
                else:
                    format_opt = "auto"
        else:
            format_opt = default_format

    format_opt = format_opt.lower()
    if format_opt not in ("auto","xz","lzma","lzip","raw"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: --format={format_opt}: Unknown file format type\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    if operation == "compress" and format_opt == "lzip":
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: Compression of lzip files (.lz) is not supported\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    if robot and operation in ("compress","decompress","test"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: Compression and decompression with --robot are not supported yet.\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    if operation == "list":
        has_real = any(f != "-" for f in files)
        if not has_real and not files_from:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: --list does not support reading from standard input\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    extra_files = []
    for fname, is_null in files_from:
        if fname is None or fname == "-":
            data = sys.stdin.read()
            if is_null:
                parts = data.split('\0')
            else:
                parts = data.split('\n')
            for p in parts:
                if p:
                    extra_files.append(p)
        else:
            try:
                with open(fname, 'r', errors='ignore') as ff:
                    content = ff.read()
                    if is_null:
                        parts = content.split('\0')
                    else:
                        parts = content.splitlines()
                    for p in parts:
                        if p:
                            extra_files.append(p)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                if quiet <2:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_basename}: {fname}: No such file or directory\n")
    files.extend(extra_files)

    if not files:
        files = ["-"]

    overall_exit = 0
    had_error = False
    had_warning = False

    def print_stderr(msg, qlevel):
        if qlevel ==0:
            sys.stderr.write(msg+"\n")
        elif qlevel==1:
            if "skipping" not in msg:
                sys.stderr.write(msg+"\n")

    def get_known_suffixes_for_compress(fmt):
        if suffix_opt is not None:
            if fmt == "xz":
                return [suffix_opt, ".xz", ".txz"]
            elif fmt == "lzma":
                return [suffix_opt, ".lzma", ".tlz"]
            else:
                return [suffix_opt]
        else:
            if fmt == "xz":
                return [".xz", ".txz"]
            elif fmt == "lzma":
                return [".lzma", ".tlz"]
            else:
                return [".xz", ".txz"]

    def get_known_suffixes_for_decompress():
        base = [".xz", ".txz", ".lzma", ".tlz"]
        if suffix_opt is not None:
            return [suffix_opt] + base
        return base

    def check_already_has_suffix(filename, fmt):
        known = get_known_suffixes_for_compress(fmt)
        for suf in known:
            if filename.endswith(suf):
                return suf
        return None

    def strip_suffix_for_decompress(filename):
        known = get_known_suffixes_for_decompress()
        for suf in known:
            if filename.endswith(suf):
                if suf in (".txz", ".tlz"):
                    prefix = filename[:-len(suf)]
                    return prefix + ".tar", suf
                else:
                    return filename[:-len(suf)], suf
        return None, None

    def get_check_const(s):
        s = s.lower()
        if s == "none":
            return lzma.CHECK_NONE
        if s == "crc32":
            return lzma.CHECK_CRC32
        if s == "crc64":
            return lzma.CHECK_CRC64
        if s == "sha256":
            return lzma.CHECK_SHA256
        return lzma.CHECK_CRC64

    def parse_filter_opts(opt_str):
        opts = {}
        if not opt_str:
            return opts
        parts = opt_str.split(',')
        for part in parts:
            part=part.strip()
            if not part:
                continue
            if "=" in part:
                k,v = part.split("=",1)
                opts[k.strip()] = v.strip()
            else:
                opts[part] = True
        return opts

    def build_filters():
        chain = []
        for bname, bopt in bcj_filters:
            bopts = parse_filter_opts(bopt)
            id_map = {
                "x86": lzma.FILTER_X86,
                "arm": lzma.FILTER_ARM,
